items.title: Twinex
items.text: A localization code generator compatible with the Twine file format, implemented in Rust.

items.title: What is Twinex?
items.text:
Twinex reads a Twine-formatted text file containing your app's translations, and generates platform-specific localization files. It also works in reverse — consuming existing localization files back into a Twine file.

GenerateConsumeValidate 
twinex generate twine.txt output/strings.xml -f android -l zh

twinex consume twine.txt zh.strings -l zh

twinex validate twine.txt --pedantic

items.title: 1. Define translations
items.text:
Create a Twine file with your base language and translations:

[[UI]]
    [btn_ok]
        comment = OK button
        en = OK
        zh = 确定
    [btn_cancel]
        comment = Cancel button
        en = Cancel
        zh = 取消

[[Errors]]
    [err_network]
        comment = Network error message
        en = A network error occurred
        zh = 网络错误

items.title: 2. Generate platform files
items.text:
# iOS
twinex generate twine.txt Localization/ -f apple -r -a

# Android
twinex generate twine.txt res/ -f android -r -a

items.title: 3. Validate
items.text: twinex validate twine.txt

items.title: Consume existing translations
items.text:
If translators provide files in platform format, merge them back:

twinex consume twine.txt translations/ -f apple -a

items.title: New
items.text:
• Documentation website powered by Zensical
  • Automated GitHub Pages deployment via GitHub Actions
  • Breaking: Consolidated 7 subcommands into 3: generate, consume, validate. Use --all/--archive flags to switch modes.
  • generate-localization-file → generate
  • generate-all-localization-files → generate --all
  • generate-localization-archive → generate --archive
  • consume-localization-file → consume
  • consume-all-localization-files → consume --all
  • consume-localization-archive → consume (auto-detected by .zip extension)
  • validate-twine-file → validate
  • Breaking: --consume-all short flag changed from -a to -c (now -a is --all for directory mode)
  • Refactored internal architecture: extracted Twinex core struct with parameter structs, decoupled from CLI parsing
  • Add cargo-dist release workflow

items.title: Fixes
items.text: • Corrected the installation command in the README from cargo install twinex to cargo install twinex-cli.

items.title: New
items.text:
• Initial release of Twinex
  • 7 subcommands: generate-localization-file, generate-all-localization-files, generate-localization-archive, consume-localization-file, consume-all-localization-files, consume-localization-archive, validate-twine-file
  • 7 output formats: Apple (.strings), Android (.xml), ARB (.arb), Django (.po), Flash (.properties), Gettext (.po), jQuery (.json)
  • Tag-based string filtering with -t and -u flags
  • Translation fallback to developer language
  • Multiple encoding support (UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-16LE, UTF-16BE)
  • Pedantic key validation mode (-p)
  • Extensible formatter registry for third-party format support

items.title: Consume
items.text: Consume existing localization files back into a Twine file.

items.title: consume
items.text:
twinex consume <TWINE_FILE> <INPUT_PATH> [OPTIONS]

The input mode is determined by the path and flags:

  • Single file (default): Consume a single localization file.
  • --all: Consume all localization files from a directory.
  • Zip archive (auto): Consume files from a zip archive (detected by .zip extension).

items.title: Single file (default)
items.text:
Consume a single localization file back into the Twine file.

twinex consume <TWINE_FILE> <INPUT_PATH> [OPTIONS]

Examples:

# Consume a Chinese strings file
twinex consume twine.txt zh.strings -l zh

# Consume and write to a new file
twinex consume twine.txt zh.xml -f android -o twine_updated.txt

# Consume all keys, add tags
twinex consume twine.txt input.xml -c -t imported

items.title: All files (--all)
items.text:
Consume all localization files from a directory.

twinex consume <TWINE_FILE> <INPUT_DIR> -a [OPTIONS]

Example:

twinex consume twine.txt Resources/ -f apple -a

items.title: Zip archive (auto)
items.text:
Consume localization files from a zip archive. Detected automatically by the .zip extension.

twinex consume <TWINE_FILE> <INPUT_ZIP> [OPTIONS]

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Description -f, --format Input format (auto-detected from extension if omitted) -l, --lang Comma-separated languages to consume -a, --all Consume all localization files from a directory -c, --consume-all Consume all keys, even if they don't exist in the Twine file -m, --consume-comments Consume comments from the localization file -d, --developer-language Override the developer language -t, --tags Tags to set on consumed definitions -o, --output-file Write the updated Twine data to a different file -e, --encoding Input file encoding

items.title: Encoding
items.text:
Twinex supports multiple output encodings:

Encoding Description UTF-8 Default encoding UTF-16 UTF-16 with BOM UTF-16LE UTF-16 little-endian UTF-16BE UTF-16 big-endian 
# Generate iOS strings with UTF-16 encoding
twinex generate twine.txt zh.strings -l zh -e UTF-16

items.title: Fallback Behavior
items.text:
When a translation is missing for a language, Twinex falls back to the developer language:

[[General]]
    [hello]
        en = Hello       ← developer language
        zh = 你好
        # ja is missing

Generating for Japanese:

"hello" = "Hello";       ← falls back to English

Set the developer language explicitly:

twinex generate twine.txt zh.strings -l zh -d en

items.title: Supported Formats
items.text:
Twinex supports 7 output formats. Each format handles reading, writing, and language detection for its platform.

Format Extension Platform apple .strings iOS / macOS android .xml Android arb .arb Flutter / Dart django .po Django flash .properties Flash gettext .po GNU Gettext jquery .json jQuery i18n

items.title: Apple
items.text:
.strings — iOS / macOS

GenerateDirectory StructureOutput Format 
twinex generate twine.txt zh.lproj/Localizable.strings -l zh

Resources/
├── zh.lproj/
│   └── Localizable.strings
└── ja.lproj/
    └── Localizable.strings

/* Apple Strings File */
"key" = "value";

Language is detected zhom the *.lproj directory name. Comments are preserved as /* ... */ blocks.

items.title: Android
items.text:
.xml — Android

GenerateDirectory StructureOutput Format 
twinex generate twine.txt res/values-zh/strings.xml -f android -l zh

res/
├── values/
│   └── strings.xml
├── values-zh/
│   └── strings.xml
└── values-ja/
    └── strings.xml

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- Android Strings File -->
<resources>
    <!-- comment -->
    <string name="key">value</string>
</resources>

Supports HTML entity encoding/decoding. Language is detected zhom values-* directory names.

items.title: ARB
items.text:
.arb — Flutter / Dart

GenerateOutput Format 
twinex generate twine.txt app_zh.arb -f arb -l zh

{
  "@@locale": "zh",
  "hello": "你好",
  "@hello": {
    "description": "A greeting"
  }
}

Comments are stored as @key.description metadata. Language is detected zhom the filename pattern *_<lang>.arb.

items.title: Django
items.text:
.po — Django

GenerateOutput Format 
twinex generate twine.txt locale/zh/LC_MESSAGES/django.po -f django -l zh

# Django Strings File
# Language: zh
#. comment
msgid "key"
msgstr "value"

items.title: Flash
items.text:
.properties — Flash

GenerateOutput Format 
twinex generate twine.txt locale/zh/resources.properties -f flash -l zh

# Flash Strings File
# Language: zh
# comment
key=value

Supports Flash-style {0}, {1} placeholder conversion.

items.title: Gettext
items.text:
.po — GNU Gettext

GenerateOutput Format 
twinex generate twine.txt messages.po -f gettext

# Gettext Strings File
# X-Generator: Twinex
# Language: zh
msgid ""
msgstr ""
"Language: zh"

#. comment
msgctxt "key"
msgid "value"
msgstr "value"

items.title: jQuery
items.text:
.json — jQuery i18n

GenerateOutput Format 
twinex generate twine.txt localize-zh.json -f jquery -l zh

{"key":"value","another":"value"}

Language is detected zhom the filename pattern *<lang>.json.

items.title: Generate
items.text: Generate localization files from a Twine file.

items.title: generate
items.text:
twinex generate <TWINE_FILE> <OUTPUT_PATH> [OPTIONS]

The output mode is determined by the flags:

  • Single file (default): Generates one localization file for a specific language.
  • --all: Generates files for all languages into a directory.
  • --archive: Generates a zip archive containing all localization files.

items.title: Single file (default)
items.text:
Generate a single localization file for a specific language and format.

twinex generate <TWINE_FILE> <OUTPUT_PATH> [OPTIONS]

Examples:

# Android XML for Chinese
twinex generate twine.txt strings.xml -f android -l zh

# iOS strings for Chinese with specific encoding
twinex generate twine.txt zh.strings -l zh -e UTF-16

# Filter by tags
twinex generate twine.txt output.xml -f android -t ios,greeting

# Only translated strings
twinex generate twine.txt zh.strings -l zh -i translated

items.title: All languages (--all)
items.text:
Generate localization files for all languages in a Twine file.

twinex generate <TWINE_FILE> <OUTPUT_DIR> -a [OPTIONS]

Example:

twinex generate twine.txt res/ -f android -r -a

This creates:

res/
├── values/
│   └── strings.xml
├── values-zh/
│   └── strings.xml
└── values-ja/
    └── strings.xml

items.title: Zip archive (--archive)
items.text:
Generate a zip archive containing all localization files.

twinex generate <TWINE_FILE> <OUTPUT_ZIP> --archive -f <FORMAT> -l <LANGS>

Example:

twinex generate twine.txt translations.zip -f apple -l zh --archive

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Description -f, --format Output format (see Supported Formats) -l, --lang Comma-separated languages to generate (default: all) -a, --all Generate all localization files (output_path is a directory) --archive Generate a zip archive of localization files -d, --developer-language Override the developer language -t, --tags Comma-separated tags to filter (e.g. ios,greeting) -u, --untagged Include strings without tags -i, --include Filter: all (default), translated, untranslated -e, --encoding Output encoding (UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-16LE, UTF-16BE) --escape-all-tags Escape all HTML/XML tags in output --validate Validate the Twine file before generating -r, --create-folders (with --all) Create language-specific directories -n, --file-name (with --all) Custom output file name

cd twinex
cargo build --release

The binary will be at target/release/twinex.

items.text: cargo install twinex-cli

items.title: The Twine File Format
items.text:
A Twine file is a plain text file that stores all your app's translations in one place. It uses indentation to define structure:

[[Section Name]]
    [key]
        comment = Developer notes about this key
        tags = ios,android
        ref = another_key
        en = English translation
        zh = Chinese translation
Attribute Description [[Section]] Groups related keys together [key] A unique identifier for a translatable string comment Optional note for translators tags Optional comma-separated tags for filtering ref Reference to another key that shares the same base translation en, zh, etc. Language code → translation value

items.title: Example
items.text:
# Define translations
cat > twine.txt << 'EOF'
[[Greetings]]
    [hello]
        en = Hello
        zh = 你好
EOF

# Generate iOS strings
twinex generate twine.txt zh.strings -l zh

# Consume back
twinex consume twine.txt zh.strings -l zh

items.title: Tag Filtering
items.text: Tags allow you to control which strings are included in generated output.

items.title: Define tags in your Twine file
items.text:
[[UI]]
    [btn_ok]
        tags = ios,android
        en = OK
    [btn_cancel]
        tags = ios
        en = Cancel
    [label_about]
        en = About

items.title: Filter by tags
items.text:
# Only strings tagged "ios"
twinex generate twine.txt output.xml -f android -t ios

# Strings tagged "ios" OR untagged strings
twinex generate twine.txt output.xml -f android -t ios -u

items.title: How it works
items.text:
In the example above:

Key Tags -t ios -t ios -u btn_ok ios,android ✓ included ✓ included btn_cancel ios ✓ included ✓ included label_about (none) ✗ excluded ✓ included
  • -t filters by tag — only strings with matching tags are included
  • -u includes untagged strings alongside tagged ones

items.title: Command Overview
items.text:
twinex <COMMAND>

Commands:
  generate  Generate localization file(s) from a twine file
  consume   Consume translations from localization file(s) into the twine file
  validate  Validate that a twine file is parseable

items.title: Generate
items.text:
Full generate reference

Mode Flag Description Single file (default) Generate a single file for one language All languages --all Generate files for all languages Zip archive --archive Generate a zip archive 
# Single file
twinex generate twine.txt output.xml -f android -l zh

# All languages
twinex generate twine.txt res/ -f android -r -a

# Zip archive
twinex generate twine.txt translations.zip -f apple -l zh --archive

Full consume reference

Mode Flag Description Single file (default) Consume a single file All files --all Consume files from a directory Zip archive (auto) Consume files from a zip archive (detected by .zip extension)

# All files in directory

items.title: Validate
items.text: Check that a Twine file is well-formed and optionally enforce naming conventions.

items.title: validate
items.text:
twinex validate <TWINE_FILE> [OPTIONS]

Examples:

# Basic validation
twinex validate twine.txt

# Pedantic mode — keys must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$
twinex validate twine.txt -p

# With developer language override
twinex validate twine.txt -d en

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Description -d, --developer-language Override the developer language -p, --pedantic Enforce key naming convention ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ -q, --quiet Suppress output
